Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank/ITU data (IT.NET.USER.ZS, sourced from the ITU) corroborates 20.01% of individuals using the internet in 2023, the latest year available for Eritrea; this falls within the 15-29% band, so Value Code 2 stands unchanged.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: GSMA Intelligence data via DataReportal (Digital 2026 report, late 2025) puts mobile connections at 23.7% of population, which sits in the <25% band (Code 1) — the original comment cited a correct figure but applied the wrong scale bucket (Code 2 requires 25-39%). Flagging for human review: GSMA's own connections estimate has swung sharply between reports (41.9% Jan 2024 to 22.2% Jan 2025 to 23.7% Oct 2025), and separate WB/ITU mobile-cellular-subscriptions-per-100 data (a different, SIM-based metric that can exceed unique subscribers) shows 59.1 in 2022, so the underlying picture is genuinely unstable for this small, state-monopoly market.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank/SDG7 Tracking data corroborates 54.4% national electrification in 2023, the latest year available, matching the 50-74% band (Code 3) unchanged.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Comments: 0.5 outages per month in firms (~6/year weekly-ish) [CEIC WB Enterprise](https://www.ceicdata.com/en/eritrea/business-environment/er-power-outages-in-firms-in-a-typical-month)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The World Bank Enterprise Survey (2009 — the only survey round ever conducted for Eritrea; no later round exists) reports 0.5 outages per month, i.e. roughly 6 per year, which fits the 'Good, <10 outages per year' band (Code 4), not 'Poor, weekly outages' (Code 2) as originally coded; the original comment misapplied its own cited figure to the scale. Flagging for human review given the data is 16 years old and no fresher firm-level survey exists.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, though close to the lower boundary. IRENA-sourced generation data (via countryeconomy.com) shows renewables at 9.9-12.0% of electricity generation across 2022-2024, consistent with the 10-24% band (Code 2).

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
Comments: Urban ~75%, rural 36%, gap ~39pp (est from 2016 urban 75%, 2022 rural 36%)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Recalculated with matched-year 2023 World Bank data: urban access 77.1% vs rural access 37.1%, a gap of 40.0 percentage points, which still falls within the 21-40pp band (Code 3). This corrects the original estimate, which mismatched a 2016 urban figure against a 2022 rural figure; the resulting code is confirmed unchanged.
